clue.text: Bigger than average chest boy's lacking

indicators.note: the chest is lacking the boy, so that word is taken off the end of it

parts.note: a tallboy is a ... chest of drawers
boy's read as 'boy is', giving the word boy

explanation.surface: A boy with an unusually large chest is somehow short of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes BOY off TALLBOY, a British name for a tall chest of drawers. Read 'boy's' as 'boy is': the chest is lacking the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall describes a person or thing of more than usual height, so bigger than the average.

clue.text: Peg holding casks up where reactions are observed

indicators.note: the peg word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a tee is the small peg a golf ball sits on

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for casks is read from bottom to top

parts.note: butts are large casks for wine or ale

explanation.surface: A peg is used to hold casks upright in a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the casks word bottom to top, as this is a down clue; 'holding' puts it inside the golf peg, after its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists watch reactions happen in a test tube, the small glass laboratory vessel.

clue.text: Parrot fashion (like rote)

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means shape or make, so these letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Copying parrot fashion, as in learning by rote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot fashion' reads as one idiom for rote learning, but 'Parrot' is the definition and 'fashion' is the anagram signal working on LIKE ROTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorikeet is a small brightly coloured parrot from Australasia, one member of the parrot family.

clue.text: They're excited by talk of orders or getting dispatched

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

parts.note: the word or is taken as written and must be dispatched from the pool

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers get excited when customers talk of orders or of goods being sent out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting dispatched' tells you OR goes: shuffle TALK OF ORDERS, remove the letters of OR, and the remaining ten letters make the answer. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's opening pronoun stands for people who trade, shopkeepers and merchants, the people the rest of the clue describes.

clue.text: One dreaded rise of a tyrant

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the letters climb upwards, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: a tsar was an autocratic Russian ruler, a byword for tyranny

explanation.surface: Someone feared the rise of a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' reverses A TSAR to give the answer. 'dreaded' looks like 'feared' but means wearing dreadlocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian is often recognised by dreadlocked hair, so is someone with dreads.

clue.text: Lorna's family acted effectively, to perform as required

parts.note: Lorna Doone, heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel, belongs to the outlaw Doone family, the Doones
bit means took hold or had an effect, as brakes or a new law bite

explanation.surface: Lorna's relatives performed well, playing their part as needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is the title character of a classic English novel set on Exmoor; her family are the Doones.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make one's own fair contribution, doing what is expected of one.

clue.text: Called time?

parts.note: read as a pub landlord calling closing time, but really a telephone service you ring that tells you the time aloud

explanation.surface: A barman calling last orders.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain you could once phone a number to hear a recorded voice announce the exact time; 'Called time' hints at a pub closing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phone service is literally time that is called up, a voice reading the hour when dialled.

clue.text: Old books containing frame of cartoon cat

indicators.note: the old-plus-books pair contains the frame word between its parts

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
a cel is one transparent celluloid frame of a hand-drawn animated cartoon

explanation.surface: Old comics include a picture of a cartoon cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' wraps the old-and-books pair round the animation frame; 'cartoon cat' tempts you towards a named character, but only 'cat' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild spotted cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Couples starting kitchens should keep something like a sausage

indicators.note: couples are pairs, so the first two letters at the start of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Kitchens should stock a sausage-like product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couples starting' takes two letters from the start of each word: KI, SH, KE.
explanation.definitionFit: Kishke is a Jewish dish of stuffed intestine or casing, much like a large sausage.

clue.text: Cropped variety is including outsize fruit like the pineapple

indicators.note: cropped means cut short, so the last letter of the variety word is lost

parts.note: a sort is a kind or variety
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A trimmed-down variety of plant produces an outsize fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cropped' trims the variety word's last letter, and 'including' wraps 'is' round the clothing-size label. A sorosis is a botanical term for a composite fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorosis is a fleshy multiple fruit formed from many flowers, the pineapple and mulberry being examples.

clue.text: Drunken fellow ends keg, being aware of own capacity

indicators.note: drunken means reeling and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunk man finishes off a keg, knowing how much he can take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' scrambles FELLOW ENDS KEG into the thirteen letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-knowledge is understanding of one's own nature and abilities, including what one can manage.

clue.text: Agreement is nothing, with assorted points the West rejected

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing
a mixed selection of compass points, using north, east and south but with west left out: N, E, N, E, S, S

explanation.surface: A deal comes to nothing as various factions spurn the West.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'points' are compass points; 'the West rejected' means no W may be used, so the mix is built from N, E and S only.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneness is unity, being in complete harmony or accord with others.

clue.text: Hear Scottish river divide and part

indicators.note: hear says the words are spoken, so what is heard is what goes in the grid

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river, and cleave means divide or split

explanation.surface: Listen to a Scottish river splitting and separating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' tells you TAY CLEAVE, said out loud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To take leave is to say goodbye and depart, so to part from someone.

clue.text: Potassium, iodine, and sulphur in fine box

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

indicators.note: the sulphur symbol goes in the word for fine

parts.note: OK means fine or all right
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Three chemical elements packed into a fine box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S between the O and K of OK; K and I come before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiosk is a small booth or stall, a box-like structure such as a phone box or news-stand.

clue.text: Inspire about a thousand to outlaw king and get maximum payout

indicators.note: the breathing word goes about the thousand, holding it

parts.note: to inspire is to breathe in
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K
to outlaw something is to ban it
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Encouraging a thousand people to banish the king and get the biggest reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the thousand inside the breathing word. 'Inspire' looks like 'motivate', but here it is breathing in; a casino's 'bank' is the money it holds to pay winners.
explanation.definitionFit: To break the bank is to win more than the casino's bank holds, the largest possible win.

clue.text: To dance, goes to ball perhaps in growth areas

parts.note: the hay is an old country dance with interweaving lines
in cricket a fielder fields, going after the ball

explanation.surface: Dancing, then off to a ball, perhaps in a booming part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side not batting fields, chasing the ball. 'ball' looks like a dance, but it is the ball being hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hayfields are meadows where grass is grown for cutting and drying, so areas of growth.

clue.text: Lose note — pounds are somewhere in room

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the two letters go somewhere inside the room word

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move
L stands for pounds, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Losing a banknote: money is somewhere in the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhere in' lets the two letters sit at any point inside the room word. The are is a metric land measure of 100 square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: To misplace something is to put it where you cannot find it, losing it for a while.

clue.text: Section of mass that's somewhat dignified, sung as offered up

indicators.note: in a down clue, offered up means the run is read upwards, so backwards
somewhat means only part of the phrase is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Part of a church service sung in a fairly stately way, as an offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes IEDSUNGA from 'dignified, sung as', and 'offered up' reverses it. The Agnus Dei is the 'Lamb of God' prayer of the Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei is one of the sung parts of the Mass, a prayer beginning 'Lamb of God'.

clue.text: Group with a supply of comprehensive apparel

parts.note: a body is an organised group of people, as in a governing body
stocking means furnishing with a supply, as a shop stocks goods

explanation.surface: An organisation supplies all-round clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' here is the verb, providing with stock, not the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A body stocking is a one-piece garment covering the whole body, so clothing that covers everything.

clue.text: Skins of holidaymakers appear hot when turning over to tan

indicators.note: turning over means the letters are flipped round, read from the end backwards
the skins of words are their outsides, so the first and last letters of each are taken

explanation.surface: Sunbathers look hot as they roll over to get a suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skins of' gives HS, AR, HT; 'when turning over' reverses the string. 'tan' is not sunburn but to beat, as in tanning someone's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: To tan someone's hide is to beat them, and thrash also means beat soundly.

clue.text: Ionised gas exploded in centre of gas-lamps

indicators.note: exploded means blown apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled
centre means the inside of the word, without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Gas from a street lamp blew up in the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes ASLAMP from GAS-LAMPS, and 'exploded' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the state of matter in which a gas is so hot its atoms have lost electrons and become charged.

clue.text: Henry and Albert killed according to law

parts.note: Hal is a pet name for Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal
Al is short for Albert

explanation.surface: Two men named Henry and Albert were executed lawfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The law is Islamic law, not a court's: the definition is about how meat is slaughtered.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal meat comes from animals slaughtered in the way Islamic law prescribes.

clue.text: Spontaneous child at play starts to trip up

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
a romp is lively play

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A small child playing begins to stumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives T and U, the first letters of 'trip' and 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: An impromptu remark or performance is done without preparation, on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: Last of lemon twist served up as cocktail ingredient

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to warp is to twist out of shape

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Garnish a cocktail with a twist of lemon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns the twist word upwards, as this is a down clue. A prawn cocktail is a starter, not a drink, so 'cocktail' misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Prawns are the main ingredient of the prawn cocktail, a classic starter in a sauce.

clue.text: Said to be moving into a place like part of church

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go into the place abbreviation

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in street names

indicators.note: moving means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rumour is said to be moving into a certain spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be moving' rearranges 'Said', and 'into' puts it inside the place abbreviation, after A. An apse is the rounded end of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Apsidal means relating to an apse, the rounded recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Unwieldy power unit in a hospital room

indicators.note: the power unit goes in between the other two pieces

parts.note: a ward is a room for patients in a hospital
kW is the kilowatt, a unit of power

explanation.surface: A clumsy power generator in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the kilowatt symbol between 'a' and the hospital room, so 'power unit' is not an electrical generator.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awkward is clumsy and hard to handle, much as an unwieldy object is.

clue.text: For Mary, Gabriel was providential

parts.note: the angel of the Annunciation came to Mary from God above, so his visit was literally dispatched from on high, and also a timely blessing

explanation.surface: The angel Gabriel's visit to Mary was a lucky stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: The archangel Gabriel was sent from heaven to tell Mary she would bear Jesus; the answer also means lucky or timely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heaven-sent comes at just the right moment as if by divine gift, so is providential.

clue.text: Head of state protected by good fairy

indicators.note: the head of state is protected inside the word for good

parts.note: pi is short for pious, so good
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, a head of state

explanation.surface: A national leader guarded by a kind fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' puts the Queen's cipher inside the word for good. 'Head of state' looks like a first-letter signal, but it is the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy or good spirit in Persian mythology.
